target.look: flat-shaded low-poly. Faceted solids, per-face flat shading, hard silhouette edges, banded warm dusk sky with hard-edged cloud slabs, warm rock in light against a chromatic blue-grey in shadow, cyan crystal and cyan water as the only saturated accents, hard-edged blocky UI, bare white KaTeX unframed in world space.
target.supersedes: reference/brief-hero.png is retained as a MOOD artefact only (colour feeling, sense of wonder). Every constant in this file is measured from target-lowpoly.png. Where the two disagree, the low-poly target wins.

howToRegenerate.guarantee: This file is machine-written. No colour in it was typed by hand. Every `measured` field names the exact box or predicate that produced it; re-run the command and the file is byte-identical.
samplingRules: Coordinates are fractions of frame width/height.
A box sample is the per-channel MEDIAN of the box - median, because a flat-shaded facet is exactly one colour and the median ignores the 1-2 px of antialiasing at its border.
A mask sample is the per-channel median of every pixel passing a stated HSV/luminance predicate inside a stated box. The predicate is the evidence; a box would be a guess.
A sky-ramp sample is the per-row median across x 0.30-0.70, which rejects cloud slabs without having to locate them.

colourSpace.rendering: linear-sRGB. `linear` is the exact sRGB->linear decode of `hex`. Feed `linear` to a shader; never feed `hex` to a linear pipeline.
colourSpace.luminance: Rec.709 relative luminance of the linear triplet (0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B).
colourSpace.three: THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = true; renderer.outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace; new THREE.Color().setHex(0xRRGGBB, SRGBColorSpace).

sky.zenith.measured: per-row median over x [0.3,0.7] at y=0
sky.zenith.allowed: Top of the sky dome. Also the colour of the hemisphere fill light — this is the only light in the rig that touches a shadowed face.

sky.high.measured: per-row median over x [0.3,0.7] at y=0.06
sky.high.allowed: Sky dome around y 0.06 of frame.

sky.pivot.measured: per-row median over x [0.3,0.7] at y=0.14
sky.pivot.allowed: The neutral crossover band where the cool upper sky becomes the warm horizon. It is the saturation minimum of the whole column and it MUST exist.
sky.pivot.forbidden: A zenith->horizon ramp that never drops below S 0.16 reads as a two-colour lerp.

sky.warm.measured: per-row median over x [0.3,0.7] at y=0.22

sky.low.measured: per-row median over x [0.3,0.7] at y=0.28

sky.horizon.measured: per-row median over x [0.3,0.7] at y=0.34
sky.horizon.allowed: Sky at the horizon line away from the sun; also the aerial-perspective target colour that all distant geometry converges to.
sky.horizon.forbidden: Never a light colour — it is the result of the key through atmosphere, not the key.

sky.horizon.antisun.allowed: The horizon on the side of frame away from the sun. The sky is 2x brighter at the sun end than at this end.

sky.sun.allowed: The sun glow at the horizon, and the key light colour.
sky.sun.forbidden: Never a lens flare with ghosts. Never a visible disc with a hard rim.

cloud.slab.allowed: The hard-edged stylised cloud slabs. Warm, flat, roughly 2x the luminance of the sky at the same altitude, and 60-110 degrees of hue away from it.
cloud.slab.forbidden: Never volumetric. Never soft-edged. Never a noise texture.

rock.lit.a.allowed: A rock facet whose normal is within ~15 degrees of the key. The brightest warm value on any solid.

rock.lit.b.allowed: Rock facet at moderate key incidence.

rock.lit.c.allowed: The value a player would name if asked what colour the rock is. The mass of the foreground.

rock.lit.d.allowed: Rock facet turning away from the key.

rock.lit.e.allowed: Rock facet at grazing key incidence — the last step before a face is in shadow.

rock.shadow.allowed: Any facet turned away from the key with sky above it. THE most important colour in this palette.
rock.shadow.forbidden: Never produced by multiplying the albedo. It is not a dark orange and it is not black: it is a chromatic blue at hue ~198 that a shadowed face of ANY albedo converges to.

rock.shadow.far.allowed: The same shadow family at mid distance — slightly lighter and less saturated, which is the whole of aerial perspective on a shadowed plane.

ground.lit.allowed: The walkable ground plane in full key. Warmer and yellower than cliff rock (hue ~43 against ~30) so the floor and the walls are different materials.

ground.bright.allowed: Ground plane closest to the key.

ground.shadow.allowed: The ground plane inside a cast shadow. It keeps its own albedo and rotates toward the fill: hue 43 -> ~123, not to the blue of a turned face.
ground.shadow.forbidden: Never the same colour as rock.shadow. An up-facing surface still sees the whole sky; a turned face does not. That difference is the only reason a cast shadow reads as a shadow rather than as a hole.

world.foliage.allowed: Ground cover, scrub, the green skirt of a shelf. Green in this world is a VALUE, not a colour.
world.foliage.forbidden: Never above S 0.45 and never above Y 0.22. A bright green reads as a UI success state, not as a plant.

world.foliage.lit.allowed: The brightest foliage in frame — a canopy or a shelf top catching the key.

crystal.hot.allowed: The bright facets of a certainty crystal. One of only two saturated cool materials in the world.
crystal.hot.forbidden: Never on rock, never on terrain, never as a general sci-fi tint.

crystal.face.allowed: The turned facets of the same crystal. A crystal shows two or three values, never a gradient.

water.core.allowed: The lit surface of a carry — the cyan river. Greener than crystal by ~3 degrees and slightly more saturated.

water.body.allowed: The shaded or deeper part of a carry, and its spill onto the bank.

hero.shadow.allowed: The character seen from the shadow side. The player is mostly THIS colour: hue ~201, the same family as rock.shadow.
hero.shadow.forbidden: Never desaturate the character to grey. The blue is what makes a low-poly figure read against warm ground.

hero.rim.allowed: The key-lit edge of the character — one or two facets on the sun side, warm and bright. This single strip is what separates the character from the ground.

hero.hair.allowed: Hair, leather, and any warm dark on the character.

hero.dark.allowed: Straps, gloves, boot soles — the near-black accents that carry the silhouette at thumbnail size.
hero.dark.forbidden: Never pure #000000; it is a cool near-black and it keeps a hue.

math.glyph.allowed: Rendered KaTeX glyphs, axis lines and plotted curves in world space. Pure white, Y 1.000, no outline, no panel, no glass.
math.glyph.forbidden: Never tinted. Never on a plate. Never given a soft glow.

math.backdrop.measured: median of {everything that is not a glyph (NOT(S<=0.12 & Y>0.75))} inside box [0.4,0.25,0.55,0.33]; n=47680 (1.1280% of frame)
math.backdrop.allowed: Not a colour to author — the measured backdrop the reference chose to hang its equation against. It is the legibility budget: see laws.glyph.

ui.ink.allowed: HUD numerals and labels. Near-white, carried by a hard dark outline rather than by a plate.

ui.outline.allowed: The outline on every UI plate, slot and glyph. Uniform width, hard, no glow, no rounding.
ui.outline.forbidden: Never a soft shadow. Never a gradient stroke.

ui.bar.health.allowed: The health meter fill. Flat, square-ended, no gradient, no gloss.

ui.bar.energy.allowed: The energy meter fill. Note it sits at hue ~197, the same family as rock.shadow — the HUD borrows the world palette rather than importing a UI blue.

ui.plate.composite.allowed: Not an authored colour: the measured RESULT of the plate over the world. Author the plate as black at the alpha in laws.uiPlate and this is what must come out.

ui.slot.fill.allowed: Item-slot interior. Warm near-black, translucent over the world.

ui.slot.bevel.allowed: The chunky neutral bevel around an item slot. Neutral grey on purpose — the one place in the frame permitted to be uncoloured.

ui.band.composite.allowed: Not an authored colour: the measured RESULT of the subtitle band over lit ground. See laws.subtitleBand.

ui.compass.composite.allowed: Not an authored colour: the measured RESULT of the compass disc over the sky.

world.grey.measured: CONSTRUCTED. The target contains no grey material. hue = hue(ground.lit); S = 0.08; V solved so luminance = sqrt(Y(ground.lit) * Y(ground.shadow)) = 0.0627. It is the only role in this file below S 0.10.
world.grey.allowed: Anything emitted by a supplied value: a sagging span, a propped roof, an approximate wall (world.md Law 5). Flat-shaded like everything else, and it is the one material with nothing bright on it anywhere.
world.grey.forbidden: Never cyan-tinted, never bloomed, never emissive. And grey does NOT take the shadow rotation: a violet or blue shadow on grey turns it back into rock.

world.grey.deep.measured: CONSTRUCTED. Same hue and S 0.068; V solved so luminance = 0.34 x Y(world.grey). Grey is the one material whose shadow does not rotate hue.
world.grey.deep.allowed: Unlit faces, undersides and contact shadows of grey objects.

ui.success.measured: CONSTRUCTED. hue 107; S and V copied from ui.bar.health (the one saturated UI colour the target does contain), so success and danger carry equal weight on screen.
ui.success.allowed: A closure landing, a claim setting, a mastery mark. Transient only.
ui.success.forbidden: Never below S 0.45 — under that it is indistinguishable from world.foliage, which never exceeds S 0.45 in the target.

keyToFill.witness: one ground plane, lit at [0.545,0.760,0.575,0.790] and inside its own cast shadow at [0.530,0.920,0.570,0.950]

facetContrastForeground.witness: one rock mass: lit plane [0.100,0.235,0.140,0.262] vs plane turned from the key [0.082,0.240,0.094,0.300]

uiPlate.witness: bar plate at [0.130,0.087,0.180,0.093] against the same world seen in the gap between the two bars at [0.130,0.0755,0.180,0.0800]

subtitleBand.witness: band at [0.325,0.860,0.350,0.872] against the same ground plane just above it at [0.325,0.833,0.350,0.843]

lightRig.status: DERIVED, not sampled. Every number here is arithmetic on two measured colours; the arithmetic is printed so it can be redone.
lightRig.fillTintDerivation: linear(ground.shadow) / linear(ground.lit), normalised to its own maximum channel. One up-facing plane, lit and in its own cast shadow, so the albedo cancels and what is left is fill/(key+fill).
lightRig.turnedFaceDerivation: linear(rock.shadow) / linear(rock.lit.c). Same shape as fillOverKey (B >> G >> R) at ~3.7x less energy, which is what a vertical, partly self-occluded face receives from the same hemisphere.

workedCalibration.keyNote: A warm white, deliberately less yellow than the sun GLOW (sky.sun) — the glow is the key seen through atmosphere, not the key.
workedCalibration.derivation: albedo = linear(brightest measured facet) / linear(key), i.e. the albedo that renders the measured facet at N.L = 1 under that key. Choose a different key and redo this division; do not copy the hex without the key it came from.

lightRig.valueLadderNote: The value ladder IS the cosine ladder. Divide each facet luminance by the brightest facet and you have N.L. A render whose facets do not sit on a cosine has either smooth normals or a tonemap doing the shading.

facetCensus.method: 4-connected flood fill, per-channel tolerance 2/255 against the seed pixel, regions of at least 0.02% of frame counted
facetCensus.note: A cliff resolves into a countable number of planes. That is the whole geometry law in one measurement.

facetEdgeWidthPx.method: horizontal scans every 7 rows over x [0.05,0.30], y [0.20,0.60]; width of a monotone run that completes a >0.15 luminance step

acutanceByDepth.method: width in px (frame is 2752 wide) of a monotone run that completes a >0.12 luminance step, on horizontal scans inside each band
acutanceByDepth.note: The near field is sharp and the far field is soft: median edge width goes 2 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 px across the depth range. That is a far-only depth of field, not a symmetric one.

horizontalScan.scan: y=0.24, x 0.1000->0.1400, inside one lit plane

verticalScan.scan: x=0.155, y 0.3410->0.3960, inside one grazing plane

withinFacetFlatness.note: A facet is EXACTLY one colour. Any shading gradient across a single face is a bug, not a nicety.

glyph.method: pure-white horizontal runs and non-glyph backdrop luminance inside box [0.40,0.25,0.55,0.33]

uiGeometry.method: vertical luminance-threshold scans: bars at x=0.15 with Y<0.030, subtitle band at x=0.31 with Y<0.045

coolAccentAboveHorizon.method: frame-wide count of {hue 150-200 & V>=0.80 & S>=0.25 & y<0.30}

luminancePercentiles.method: every 2nd pixel in x and y of the whole frame

coolAccentShareOfFrame.note: Pixels at hue 150-200, V>=0.80, S>=0.25. The reference spends 0.94% of frame on saturated cyan and NOTHING ELSE in the frame is allowed into that gate. Below 0.4% the world stops having a subject; above 1.8% the accent stops being an accent.

warmLitShareOfFrame.note: Pixels at hue 20-50, S>=0.40, Y>=0.08. Warm rock is the mass of the picture.

coolShadowShareOfFrame.note: Pixels at hue 170-220, Y<=0.06. If this is near zero the render has no shadow direction; if it is over 0.16 the frame has gone gloomy.

blownShareOfFrame.note: Y>=0.90. In the reference this is the sun glow plus the KaTeX plus crystal cores, and nothing else.

crushedShareOfFrame.note: Y<=0.004. Shadows are chromatic; a render that crushes more than 1.2% of frame to near-black has lost the palette.

greenShareOfFrame.note: hue 60-150, S>=0.25. Almost all of it is dark ground cover and cast shadow.
